item.title: Write Narration From The Clip

turns.text: Watch this and write a short English voice-over explaining what's happening. Replace the original conversation with your narration, friendly and matter-of-fact. Keep all 10 seconds of footage unchanged, with no music or captions. You pick the wording and voice.

item.tests: Tests deriving a grounded narration from an attached clip and delivering it mixed into the original video with the original dialogue removed.

answer_sheet.What the narration should describe: The two coworkers discussing the new schedule, including the Monday start time of nine.
answer_sheet.Original sound: Remove the original conversation and replace it with narration.
answer_sheet.Video duration and framing: Keep all 10 seconds and preserve the source framing and sequence.
answer_sheet.Music, captions, and lip synchronization: No music or captions; do not alter the footage to match the narrator's mouth movements.

must_haves: The final video retains the original two coworkers, office setting, shot sequence, and 10-second duration.
An intelligible English narrator explains that the coworkers are discussing a schedule change and that Mondays now start at nine.
The narration does not invent names, job roles, or additional schedule changes unsupported by the clip.
The original man-and-woman conversation is no longer audible beneath the narration.
The narration fits within the video without a clipped ending, and no music or captions are added.

turns.text: Watch this clip and write a short English voice-over explaining what's happening. Replace the original conversation with your narration, friendly and matter-of-fact. Keep all 10 seconds of footage unchanged, with no music or captions. You pick the wording and voice. I'm on the free plan and don't want my credits burned, so tell me what it will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do this?

dialog.agent:
**I haven’t run any generation or spent any credits.**

Your request needs two things: a spoken narration track, then an audio-only replacement that leaves every frame of the 10-second video untouched. The connected tools don’t offer standalone text-to-speech plus audio replacement. Video editing or lip-sync would risk changing the footage, so I wouldn’t use them for this.

I also can’t watch the clip from its Magic Hour file path with the available tools, so I shouldn’t invent what’s happening.

### Cost and cheaper options
- **Exact Magic Hour cost:** I can’t quote a supported price for this operation with the tools available.
- **Cheapest suitable route: 0 Magic Hour credits.** Use a free local video editor, mute the original audio, and add either a recorded narration or a free text-to-speech track. Keep the full 10 seconds, with no music or captions.
- **Shorter or smaller?** Neither is necessary to save Magic Hour credits on that route. Trimming would violate your full-length requirement; lowering resolution would reduce image quality without helping the narration task.

Provide a playable version I can inspect, or briefly describe the action, and I can write a friendly, matter-of-fact English script timed for 10 seconds. I’d choose a neutral, conversational voice at a relaxed pace.
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with the cheapest option you listed

dialog.agent:
The cheapest route uses **0 Magic Hour credits**, but I can’t operate a local editor or replace the audio directly with the connected tools.

First, please **describe what happens in the clip**, including any important actions. I can then write a friendly narration timed to fit all 10 seconds—without guessing.

To finish for free, you can record that script on your phone, mute the original conversation in a free video editor, and add the recording. Keep the video at its original length and resolution, with music and captions off.
dialog.user: The clip shows two coworkers discussing the new schedule, including the Monday start time of nine. Pick the narration wording and voice; keep it friendly and matter-of-fact.

turns.agent:
**Narration:**  
“Two coworkers are going over the new schedule. They discuss the details, including the nine o’clock start time on Monday.”

**Voice:** A warm, neutral English voice, spoken clearly at a relaxed, conversational pace to fit the 10-second clip.

No generation has run, and **no Magic Hour credits have been spent**. The script is ready to record and use in place of the original audio, keeping all footage unchanged with no music or captions.
